notes.meaning: God reveals himself to people who had not been seeking him, welcoming the Gentiles into his covenant. The apostle Paul explains in Romans 10:20 that this showed God taking the first step to save outsiders. His free mercy reaches out to those who did not even know to ask for him.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest the original words spoke of wayward Israel acting like the heathen, rather than predicting the calling of the Gentiles.

notes.meaning: God patiently reached out to Israel day after day, holding out his hands like an earnest parent calling a stubborn child home. Yet the people refused his invitation and walked down evil paths. They preferred to follow their own sinful desires instead of obeying God's word.

The people constantly sinned right in front of God, showing no fear of his holy presence. They took part in pagan rituals in sacred groves and burned incense on unauthorized brick altars. By turning away from God's appointed altar, they openly insulted him.

The people practiced dark rituals by sitting among graves and hiding in secret caves to consult the dead. They also broke God's law by eating pork and drinking impure broth from unclean sacrifices. These acts showed how deeply they had adopted heathen customs.

Even while doing these unclean things, the people proudly told others to keep their distance, claiming to be far holier than anyone else. This self-righteous hypocrisy was deeply offensive to the Lord. He describes their false piety as irritating smoke in his nose that provokes his anger all day long.

God has a full written record of their evil deeds and will not remain silent forever. Though he was patient for a long time, the day of judgment has been decreed. He will pay them back directly and fully for all their rebellions.

The Lord will judge both this generation and their ancestors together because the children repeated the sins of their fathers. For generations they had worshiped idols on high hills and mountain shrines, which was an open insult to God. Now the full penalty for their long history of idolatry will be poured into their laps.

When a worker finds a single cluster of good, juicy grapes on a failing vine, he spares the vine because it still holds a blessing. In the same way, the Lord will not destroy the entire nation of Israel. For the sake of the faithful few who truly serve him, he will preserve a remnant.

God promises to bring forth faithful descendants out of Jacob and heirs out of the tribe of Judah. His chosen servants will return to inherit the promised land. They will safely live upon his holy hills and worship him there in peace.

The land will be completely restored from the fertile coastal plain of Sharon in the west to the Valley of Achor in the east. The Valley of Achor, once famous for trouble and Achan's sin, will become a peaceful pasture for cattle. God reserves this fruitful land for those who truly seek him.

God confronts the rebels who turned away from his temple on Mount Zion. Instead of worshiping him, they prepared feasts and mixed wine offerings for Fortune and Destiny, the false gods of luck and fate. They looked to superstition rather than trusting the living God.

Because they worshiped the false god of destiny, the Lord himself will appoint their destiny to fall by the sword. God called out to them through his prophets, but they refused to answer or listen. They deliberately chose to do what was wicked in his sight.

The Lord reveals the stark contrast between his faithful followers and those who rebel against him. God's true servants will be fed and satisfied, while the wicked will suffer bitter hunger and thirst. Those who love the Lord will rejoice, but the rebellious will be put to open shame.

God's servants will sing aloud with hearts full of gladness because of his goodness. On the other hand, the ungodly will weep and groan in anguish under God's righteous punishment. Their stubborn rebellion will end in grief and a crushed spirit.

The names of the wicked will become a warning and a curse among God's chosen people, remembered only as an example of ruin. The Lord will put these rebels to death for their unfaithfulness. At the same time, he will give his faithful servants a brand new name that reflects his blessing.

Anyone seeking a blessing or making a solemn promise in the land will do so by the God of truth, who always keeps his word. Idols will be completely abandoned in favor of the one true God. The old sins, heartaches, and troubles will be wiped away and entirely forgotten.

The Lord announces that he will create a brand new heaven and a brand new earth. This complete renewal will bring lasting peace and righteousness. The former troubles, sorrows, and sins of the old world will fade from memory and never come to mind again.

differ.view: This verse looks ahead to the final new creation after the end of time, while the verses that follow describe a temporary earthly kingdom.
The new heavens and new earth picture the spiritual renewal of the world that began through Christ and the gospel church.

notes.meaning: God commands his people to be glad and celebrate forever in what he is making. He will fashion Jerusalem into a place of pure celebration and make its people a constant joy. The new community of faith will live in unending praise.

God himself will take deep personal pleasure in his redeemed people and their city. All the grief and mourning that once filled their lives will come to an end. The sound of crying and weeping will never be heard there again.

Life will be so rich and full that babies will no longer die in infancy, and old men will live out their full years. Dying at one hundred years of age will be considered dying in childhood, and only someone under God's judgment would fail to reach that milestone. Untimely deaths and disasters will no longer rob families of life.

differ.view: Because physical death and sinners are still mentioned here, this describes an earthly thousand-year kingdom of Christ rather than the final eternal state.
This language uses the image of very long life as a poetic symbol for the abundant, flourishing spiritual life believers receive in the church.

notes.meaning: The people will build houses and live in them safely without fear of being driven away. They will plant vineyards and eat their own harvest in peace. God promises that their hard work will produce lasting blessings for them to enjoy.

The old curse of building homes or planting crops only for foreign invaders to steal them is completely reversed. God's chosen people will live long, sturdy lives like strong trees. They will live long enough to wear out and thoroughly enjoy the works of their own hands.

Parents will no longer work in vain or face the sorrow of seeing their children carried away by sudden calamity, war, or illness. Their families will be recognized as people blessed by the Lord. This divine blessing will rest upon both parents and their children for generations to come.

The relationship between God and his people will be wonderfully close and personal. Even before they finish voicing their prayers, the Lord will already answer them. He knows their needs ahead of time and delights in giving them help without delay.

Wild animals will live together in peaceful harmony, with wolves feeding beside lambs and lions eating straw like cattle. The ancient curse remains on the serpent, showing that evil and Satan are completely defeated and brought low. On God's holy mountain, no harm or violence will ever exist again.
